i tweaked my definitions of cryptids, critters, and varmints to be the following:
cryptids: big scary creatures, can be friendly but intelligent and powerful (Champ)
critters: small creatures, may have some small plot relevance but will mostly be used for flavor. not intended for combat (Dream Sparrows)
varmints: homebrew creatures that will engage in combat but aren't the big deal fights that cryptids are and can be affected by stuff like *prot from evil and good* (Shadow Beasts)

DM Mariam's simple guide to dealing with messing up pronouns:
Oh shoot, you messed up another player's or character's pronouns/name! You want to respect them and try your best, but you accidently did the wrong thing!
Well I'm here to help. As a real life trans person (tm), I can give you my advice on this situation. 
1: apologize
The most important way to make sure someone knows you care about their pronouns is by making clear you know when you did wrong. If you didn't realize and someone else points it out, this step is still important.
2: say the phrase again
Practice makes perfect. And if you want to practice using the correct pronouns, there's no better way than re-doing the statement. Because if your brain knows not only that you made a mistake, but what the right thing to say was, it'll make it easier to get it right the next time.
If you typed out the mistake, please edit the message to use the correct pronouns.
3: don't make a big deal out of it.
I promise you, we want to move on just as much as you do. Acknowledging the mistake and moving on is all we need to hear to know you're working on it. Don't make it any more awkward then it needs to be.

That's it! Here's an example to help you understand what the steps mean. Let's say you're talking in out of character about something I mentioned yesterday that has implications for your character.

You: "Yeah, DM Mariam mentioned something yesterday about missing children posters in another Burrough. I wonder what he's trying to set up with that."
Someone else: "She."
You: "Oh my bad, sorry. I wonder what she's trying to set up with that."
Me: "You'll have to find out..."

And just like that, we've moved on and you've given your brain more practice! Easy!

This has been DM Mariam's simple guide to dealing with messing up pronouns.
